relevance_note: Case report of one female with Danon disease and a LAMP2 variant: "The patient carried a novel de novo mutation, LAMP2 c.2T>C located at the initiation codon."
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a Python script in the scratch directory assembled the JSON and located each span in the paper (mapping Unicode hyphens and thin spaces only to find the exact original text). Table 1 has the patients as columns, headers 'Proband', "Proband's father", "Proband's mother"; data columns start after the row label (and, in the lab section, after a 'Reference ranges' column). Labels: 'Proband' is a role word, so the single patient is 'patient' (rule 5) and the parents 'father of patient' / 'mother of patient'. The parents tested negative ('Mutation: None') and get no variant rows. Transcript left 'not reported': NM_013995.2 is printed only for the LAMP2 cDNA used in the plasmids, not as the reference for c.2T>C. Lab values in Table 1 within the printed reference range (CK, AST, ALT) were recorded as excluded 'elevated' findings with the table row (including the reference range) as span; the text does not call them normal in words. Parents' NT-proBNP and TnI values below the printed reference range were not recorded; parents' echo values (no interpretation given) were not recorded. Normal ECG (parents; and patient's ECG at the time of syncope as recalled by parents) and normal head CT recorded only as 'abnormal ECG'/'abnormal head CT' excluded, nothing more specific (D-27). The recalled normal ECG at syncope sits beside abnormal ECGs two years earlier and at admission; not treated as a contradiction because they are different occasions. Checklist 'intellectual disability, cognitive impairment or learning difficulties' left not reported for all three: normal WAIS-RC and 'mental retardation were not found' do not address learning difficulties (narrow vs broad rule); the exclusions are in phenotypic_features. Abstract says the patient is heterozygous by implication only; zygosity taken from the Discussion sentence about this patient ('heterozygous null mutation'). Variant type 'missense' as the authors state, though they also call it null. Minor inconsistency: Results say approximately 20% of the mRNA was degraded, later 'approximately 80% reduction in mRNA'; not used for any field. No stacked cells.

functional_evidence_statement.value: Reduced LAMP2 mRNA and protein in patient PBMCs (haploinsufficiency); mutant plasmid in HEK293 gave no EGFP fusion protein (new initiation codon at first downstream ATG, six amino acids); impaired late autophagic flow in mCherry-GFP-LC3 assay; 28% mutant transcripts in leukocytes, XCI not skewed
span: The quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) and Western blot (WB) analysis of peripheral blood leukocytes from the patients revealed evidence of LAMP2 haploinsufficiency.
WB results confirmed this conclusion and no EGFP protein was detected in the LAMP2_Mut group (Figure 5f).
Laser confocal results showed increased yellow fluorescence in LAMP2_Mut compared with LAMP2 WT (Figure 6), suggesting impairing late‐stage autophagic flow.
The results showed that 28% (14/50) of mutant transcripts remained active in the patient's leukocytes (Figure 7b).
Although the translation was restarted, only six amino acids were translated.

pathogenicity_as_stated_by_authors.span: ACMG guidelines classify the novel mutation as most likely pathogenic (PVS1−moderate + PS2 + PM2)
